description: Necesitamos gente que sea capaz de explicar sobre el espacio a niños pequeños
summary:
Our team aimed to develop an interactive website focused on addressing the challenge “Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Stories About Discarded NASA Equipment on the Moon and Mars.” The main objective was to design an engaging and accessible platform for children between the ages of 6 and 12, allowing them to learn about and understand the scientific and technological advancements humanity has achieved through space exploration.

Our project addresses this topic through interactive and dynamic resources that explain the history, characteristics, and significance of the hardware and equipment left on the lunar and Martian surfaces as a result of various space missions. In this way, we aim to transform scientific information into an educational and entertaining experience, making it easier for children to understand while stimulating their curiosity about the universe, technology, and space exploration.

The importance of this project lies in its contribution to science communication and the promotion of scientific and technological interest from an early age. We believe that interactive digital tools can bring scientific knowledge closer to younger generations, encouraging them to develop curiosity, creativity, and an interest in humanity's discoveries and technological achievements in space exploration.
details:
The project consists of the development of an interactive website designed to provide information about the hardware and equipment that have been left on the surface of the Moon and Mars as a result of NASA's space missions. Through digital and interactive resources, the platform presents scientific and historical information in an educational and engaging way, helping children between the ages of 6 and 12 understand the importance of this equipment in space exploration.

The main benefit of this project is to facilitate access to scientific knowledge through an educational digital tool. Additionally, it encourages children to develop curiosity about science, technology, and space exploration. It also contributes to independent learning, stimulates imagination, and promotes interest in STEM fields (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics).

The project is expected to have a positive educational impact on future generations by fostering an early interest in scientific research and technological advancements. Furthermore, it aims to contribute to the dissemination of space exploration history, demonstrating that even equipment that is no longer operational or remains on other celestial bodies is part of humanity's scientific and technological development.

For the development of our project, we used HTML (HyperText Markup Language) and CSS (Cascading Style Sheets). HTML was used to structure and organize the website's content, including text, images, and different informational sections. On the other hand, CSS was used to define the platform's visual design by implementing styles, colors, typography, element layouts, and formatting to improve its presentation and user experience.

The creativity of this project lies in transforming a scientific and historical topic, such as abandoned hardware on the Moon and Mars, into an interactive digital experience designed specifically for children. Instead of presenting only technical information, the project aims to communicate scientific knowledge through visual and dynamic elements that make learning more engaging and entertaining.

Additionally, it explores a lesser-known perspective of space exploration: the significance of objects and equipment that remain on other planets and natural satellites after space missions have been completed.

During the development of the project, our team primarily considered the following factors:

  • Target audience: Adapting the content to children between the ages of 6 and 12.
  • Accessibility: Developing a platform that is simple and easy to use.
  • Interactive design: Incorporating visual and dynamic elements that facilitate the learning process.
  • Scientific content: Providing relevant information related to NASA's space missions.
  • Educational value: Promoting interest in science, technology, and space exploration.
  • User experience: Ensuring that website navigation is intuitive, engaging, and appropriate for the target age group.
